_readme: Every parameter: lo = conservative (fewer riders / smaller market), base, hi = aggressive. tag: FACT (public, verified, cited in research/03-market-size.md), ESTIMATE (derived from several sources), ASSUMPTION (no direct evidence; replace with HMP data or field tests). Sources are abbreviated; full citations in research/03-market-size.md and research/raw/market/.

restaurants_target_zone.note: LA County DPH Restaurant & Market Inventory (2026-07), restaurant program elements deduped to facilities, point-in-polygon: Downtown LA NC + Arts District/Little Tokyo NC 910, Wilshire Center-Koreatown NC 611, Westlake N+S NC 104, Pico Union NC 126, Empowerment Congress North (USC) 211

restaurants_radius_3mi.note: same source, 3-mile circle around 768 Ceres (34.0363, -118.2447); circle is 91% City of LA; Vernon (own health dept) missing

restaurants_city_la.note: same source, union of 99 Neighborhood Council polygons

restaurants_county_la.note: same source, all LA County (excl. Pasadena, Long Beach, Vernon which run own health departments)

restaurants_sf_core.note: SF DPH inspections 2024-present (tvy3-wexg), RESTAURANT/TAKE-OUT/FAST FOOD permits, SoMa+Mission+Tenderloin+FiDi/South Beach analysis neighborhoods

nyc_weekly_active_couriers.note: NYC DCWP Nov 2022: 61,000 working in any given week (Q2 2022); Mayor 2024-07: 'more than 60,000'; NYSERDA Dec 2025: 'over 65,000'

nyc_deliveries_per_courier_week.note: DCWP: 124M deliveries/yr (2021-22) / 52 / 61,000 = 39; Q4 2024: 2.72M deliveries/wk / 60k trip-performing accounts = 45 (accounts not deduped)

la_orders_per_restaurant_vs_nyc.note: NYC ~0.33 deliveries/resident/week (2.77M/wk / 8.48M) vs US average ~0.11 (DoorDash 'over 3M/day' US 2024 / ~0.62 share / 340M). LA assumed 1.2-1.8x US average -> 0.4-0.6 of NYC per capita; restaurants per capita similar in both (2.7 vs 2.9 per 1,000). Also consistent with DoorDash two-wheel miles LA 38.3M vs NYC 45.2M at 49% vs 55% shares (city label boundary undefined)

la_deliveries_per_courier_week.note: per weekly-active courier. NYC career couriers 39-45; Seattle all on-demand apps 12.7 offers/account-week; DoorDash national average Dasher ~4 hrs/wk x ~1.5/hr = ~6. LA blend of car-based casual majority and full-time minority (Berkeley 2024: 12% of CA delivery drivers full-time, 59% of trips by 20+ hr/wk drivers). lo = higher productivity = fewer couriers

weekly_to_daily_active.note: no source publishes daily/weekly. DoorDash: avg 4 hrs/wk in 2-3 hr sessions -> 0.2-0.35; NYC full-timers 6+ days/wk -> ~0.85; blend weighted by hours (heavy users do most hours)

zone_order_intensity_vs_county.note: app orders per restaurant in DTLA/Ktown/Westlake/USC vs LA County average: dense residential + office lunch + late-night; DPH counts in DTLA include hotel/stadium/institutional kitchens which pulls the other way

doordash_us_deliveries_per_day.note: DoorDash Dash Report 2025 (2024 data): 'over 3 million deliveries per day' US; FY2025 global Total Orders 3,172M (+23%, ex-Deliveroo +20% in Q4) -> 2025 US 3.3-4.0M/day

doordash_us_share.note: Bloomberg Second Measure Mar 2024: DoorDash 67% of US meal-delivery sales, Uber Eats 25% (incl. Postmates), Grubhub 8%; 2025-26 aggregators 56-61%. lo = higher share = smaller total market

la_county_share_us_orders.note: LA County 9.76M / US 340.1M = 2.87% population share x intensity 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.45 (DoorDash: 'Greater Los Angeles' is its highest-volume metro; warm climate; but car-based)

orders_per_courier_day.note: per daily-active courier: NYC 2.72M/wk over ~49k daily-active (61k x 0.8) = ~8/day even with career riders; Gridwise 2025 median 1.5-1.7 deliveries per active hour; LA car couriers 1.5-2.5/hr x 4-7 hrs. lo = more productive = fewer couriers

ca_app_based_workers_quarter_active.note: UC Riverside CEFD Feb 2022: 800,000 CA drivers completed >=1 ride/delivery in Q3 2021 across DoorDash+Instacart+Lyft+Uber (two-thirds <5 hrs/wk); Flex/Public First: 870,000 'active' CA app workers (2022). Grown modestly to 2025

la_county_share_ca_gig.note: LA County = 24.85% of CA population (DOF 2026), 26.6% of CA NAICS 722 employment (QCEW Jun 2025), 26.2% of CA NAICS 492 nonemployer couriers (Census 2023: 44,977 of 171,603)

delivery_share_of_app_workers.note: share of quarter-active CA app workers who do food/goods delivery rather than only rideshare; DoorDash alone reports 8M+ annual US Dashers vs Uber+Lyft ~2M US drivers, so delivery is the majority of app workers

quarterly_to_weekly_active.note: NYC DCWP: 61,000 weekly / 122,104 quarterly-unique = 0.50; Seattle OLS: ~13.7k weekly unique / 34,646 quarterly = ~0.40; DoorDash: typical Dasher active ~10 of 52 weeks, 73% dash <4 weeks per quarter -> ~0.25-0.30

la_two_wheel_delivery_share.note: DoorDash 2026 Two-Wheeled Progress Report p.7: Los Angeles, CA 49% of deliveries on two wheels (2025, two-month window, 'approximate'; city boundary undefined). Uber Eats LA unknown and likely lower (scooter mode capped at <50cc) -> blended 40-49%

two_wheel_delivery_to_courier_share.note: two-wheel couriers do more deliveries per hour (DoorDash: +10%/hr; NYC e-bike 2.03 vs car 1.13) and more hours, so courier share < delivery share. NYC: non-car 56% of workers vs 78% of deliveries (0.72); DoorDash LA gap smaller -> 0.8-0.95

zone_two_wheel_uplift.note: dense core (DTLA/Ktown/Westlake/USC) vs LA-wide 49%; SF citywide 72%, Oakland 63%; DoorDash: two-wheel trips under 2 miles in dense cores >=10% faster than cars. No neighborhood data exists

ebike_emoped_share_of_two_wheel.note: NYC intercept (NYSERDA 2025): personal e-bike 48% + rental e-bike 24% + e-moped 7% = 79% electric, gas moped 13%, pedal 5%. LA: Uber Eats scooter mode (<50cc gas) and cheaper used gas scooters push gas share up; no LA data

gas_scooter_share_of_two_wheel.note: gas 49-150cc scooters and motorcycles; NYC 13% gas moped; Craigslist LA snapshot: 50-150cc scooters $899-2,795, one explicit 'delivery scooter'. lo = more gas = fewer HMP-type riders

two_wheel_serviceable_share.note: share of two-wheel couriers HMP could sell or rent to (e-bike riders as upgrade/rental, gas riders as conversion, pedal riders as upgrade); excludes riders on employer/rental fleets, kids' bikes, walking

car_convertible_share.note: share of car couriers in the zone who would switch to two wheels within 24 months; critics: 2-8% realistic vs 20-30% implied; DoorDash Chicago/Whizz program converted 'more than 150' car Dashers city-wide

reachable_share_768ceres.note: share of zone riders who would use a hub at 768 Ceres: DTLA/Little Tokyo/Arts District/Fashion District within 1.5 mi (~50% of zone restaurants) high; Koreatown 4-5 mi, Westlake 3.3 mi, USC 3 mi low; Skid Row edge after dark

penetration_m12.note: share of SAM (weekly-active people) that are paying HMP customers by month 12; SF reached 600-1,000 vehicles in ~25 months against an SF two-wheel weekly-active pool plausibly 3-9k -> 10-30% at month 25

penetration_m24.note: by month 24; upper end = SF-like community dynamics replicate

hmp_sf_active_customers.note: HMP: >1,000 vehicles sold, 300+ battery subscribers, ~100 on rent; Gazetteer SF 2026-04-02: 'over 600 e-mopeds in SF, targeting 1,000 by year-end'. Active = vehicles in regular use

sf_two_wheel_courier_share.note: SF 72% of DoorDash deliveries on two wheels (2025) x delivery-to-courier factor 0.75-0.9. lo = higher SF share = LA looks relatively smaller

la_maturity_vs_sf_at_m24.note: LA hub at month 24 vs SF store at ~25 months (registered 2024-08): no founder on site, no seeded referral network, Spanish/Korean-speaking communities, no walk-in

la_two_wheel_miles_per_day_doordash.note: DoorDash 2026 Two-Wheeled Progress Report p.7: Los Angeles, CA 38,304,846 two-wheel miles in a two-month 2025 window (/61 days). SF 21,413,128 (351k/day); NYC 45,238,991 (742k/day)

county_share_of_doordash_label_miles.note: DoorDash does not define the 'Los Angeles, CA' boundary. If it is the metro, LA County holds ~75% of population but more of the dense two-wheel activity; if it is the city, county >= label (capped at 1.0)

miles_per_two_wheel_courier_day.note: on-app miles per daily-active two-wheel courier incl. cruising; NYC avg delivery 1.77 mi but LA legs 2-5 mi (ShiftTracker); full-time e-moped rider 8 hrs x ~8-12 mph effective = 60-100 mi; casual riders far less. lo = more miles = fewer couriers

doordash_share_of_two_wheel_couriers_la.note: DoorDash ~60-67% of US meal-delivery sales (Second Measure 2024); Uber Eats two-wheel share in LA likely lower (scooter mode <50cc), so DoorDash's share of two-wheel couriers is above its order share. lo = higher share = fewer total

nyc_miles_calibration.note: applying the same miles route to NYC (742k two-wheel mi/day / 40-60 mi = 12-18k) overshoots the DCWP-implied DoorDash two-wheel daily-active (~8k: 61-65k weekly x ~0.28 DoorDash NYC share x 0.55 two-wheel x 0.85 daily/weekly) by 1.5-2.3x -> multiply LA result by 0.45-0.65; hi allows the NYC label to be metro-wide
